correctness.rationale: Exact signed jump-measure representation for canonical BV reduces norm to single-jump responses. Strict convexity gives a finite 2n-endpoint formula; binomial moderate-deviation bounds control boundary jumps and justify uniform CLT localization. The Gaussian coefficient is globally maximized at s=1/2. The ratio of Laplace integrals A(alpha)/B(alpha) is strictly increasing because their logarithmic arguments are on opposite sides of log2, giving the unique optimizer. Pointwise Gaussian algebra gives c(1)=c(2) and the exact improvement window. Numerical checker independently sampled direct responses, degree-one formula and asymptotic trends; not substituted for proofs.

value.rationale: The intrinsic Bézier tail-power is a natural approximation design parameter and the exact sharp integrated BV error is a meaningful stability invariant for discontinuous data. The theorem supplies a complete global parameter comparison, proves a unique optimal setting, gives a nontrivial 5.06% leading-error reduction, demonstrates a finite-degree-to-asymptotic reversal, and provides reproducible exact finite-degree maximization. It is not a parameter renaming or an arbitrary low-degree table; no downstream theorem is assumed.
